page.title: Weekly Mental Check
page.subtitle: A private self-reflection tool. Answer honestly — there are no right or wrong responses.
page.description: The Mental Check is based on the international PHQ-9 questionnaire and helps assess your level of low mood.
page.disclaimer: This tool is for self-reflection and does not provide medical diagnosis.

form.rateLimitError: You have already submitted a check-in in the last 24 hours. Please try again tomorrow.

questions.q0: Little interest or pleasure in doing things
questions.q2: Trouble falling or staying asleep, or sleeping too much
questions.q3: Feeling tired or having little energy
questions.q5: Feeling bad about yourself — or that you are a failure or have let yourself or your family down
questions.q6: Trouble concentrating on things, such as reading the newspaper or watching television
questions.q7: Moving or speaking so slowly that other people could have noticed, or the opposite — being so fidgety or restless that you have been moving around a lot more than usual
questions.q8: Thoughts that you would be better off dead, or of hurting yourself in some way

summary.minimal: Your responses suggest minimal symptoms. Continue caring for your wellbeing with healthy routines.
summary.mild: Your responses suggest mild symptoms. Consider small lifestyle adjustments and monitor how you feel over the coming days.
summary.moderate: Your responses suggest moderate symptoms. It may be helpful to speak with a mental health professional for additional support.
summary.moderately-severe: Your responses suggest moderately severe symptoms. Reaching out to a mental health professional is encouraged.
summary.severe: Your responses suggest severe symptoms. Please consider connecting with a mental health professional as soon as possible.

crisisNotice: If these thoughts become stronger or more frequent, consider contacting a mental health professional or a support line in your area.
